brief: October nonfarm payrolls rose 165k, well above MS's 60k estimate and the 70k consensus, with prior months revised up a net 84k. Private payrolls (+159k) accelerated to a 126k three-month average from 82k over six months, driven by a 70k jump in professional/business services and 55k in health and social services. Aggregate payroll incomes rose at a 5.7% annualized rate versus 3Q, up from ~4.0% in the prior two quarters. The unemployment rate fell to 4.14% from 4.18%, but would have dropped further (to 3.95%) absent a labor-force-participation rise concentrated among workers 55 and older, which MS calls volatile. Wage growth kept decelerating (AHE 3.1% y/y vs 3.9% a year earlier), with services wages slowing more than goods; MS attributes most of this to compositional shift rather than falling wage rates, per the ECI. MS's ~50k/month breakeven pace estimate holds as 3- and 6-month averages reaccelerate. The only soft spot: production-worker hours fell 0.2% m/m. Net: the report keeps the Fed on track for a December hike, even as claims, JOLTs, hiring plans and ADP ran softer.
